final_answer:
CLOSING CHECKLIST DEVIATION REPORT
Asset Purchase Agreement dated March 14, 2025 (Saxonbrook / Cascade Precision Components, LLC) vs. Closing Checklist dated April 28, 2025 (Whitfield & Crane LLP)
Privileged and confidential. Scope: the two supplied documents only; no external law was needed. Full-form exhibits and Disclosure Schedules were not supplied.

1. METHOD, RATING KEY AND BOTTOM LINE
Under Checklist Part VIII, the APA controls on any discrepancy. Every deviation below is therefore a checklist error to correct, unless it is flagged as an APA drafting defect.
Severity: CRITICAL = would cause a wrong payment, a missed closing condition or deliverable, or a waived right. HIGH = wrong economics, term or deadline that is likely to be relied on. MEDIUM = incorrect description or cross-reference that risks a defective document. LOW = clerical.

Bottom line. The checklist's economic terms track an earlier or different deal. The Escrow Amount, Closing Cash Payment, Holdback percentage, General Cap, Escrow Period, Outside Date, TSA fee and Non-Compete term are all wrong against the executed APA. The checklist also omits three Seller deliverables (FIRPTA, estoppels, title commitments), the Northwind consent (a closing condition) and the Washington good standing certificate. Funds flow, docketing and closing certificates built from the checklist as written would be wrong. The APA also has internal defects that need a written fix before closing (Section 6).

2. ECONOMIC AND FUNDS-FLOW DEVIATIONS
D-1 CRITICAL. Escrow Amount. Checklist: $5,500,000 (Parts I, V (B-1, B-4), VI (PC-3)). APA: $5,250,000, which is 6% of the Purchase Price (Section 1.1 "Escrow Amount"; 2.5(b)(ii); 8.2(b); 9.5; Exhibit F). The checklist figure is about 6.29%.
D-2 CRITICAL. Closing Cash Payment. Checklist: $78,500,000. APA: $78,750,000 (Section 1.1; 2.5(b)(i); 8.2(a)). The checklist therefore understates the payment to Seller by $250,000. The total of the two wires is $84,000,000 under both documents, so the error is a split error that a total-only check would not catch.
D-3 HIGH. Holdback percentage. Checklist: 5%. APA: 4% ($3,500,000 / $87,500,000 = 4%) (Section 1.1; 2.5(b)(iii)). The dollar amount matches.
D-4 HIGH. General Indemnification Cap. Checklist: $8,500,000. APA: $8,750,000, which is 10% (Section 1.1; 9.4(c)). The checklist figure is only 9.7%.
D-5 HIGH. Escrow Period and release date. Checklist: 24 months, released about May 15, 2027. APA: 18 months, expiring November 15, 2026 (Section 1.1; 9.5; Exhibit F). This also matches the general survival period. The checklist's reference to Article X is wrong; indemnification is Article IX. Action: re-docket the release and claim-notice cutoff to November 15, 2026. The Escrow Agent would otherwise be instructed with the wrong term. Buyer should have claims noticed before that date, since the escrow secures indemnity.
D-6 HIGH. Working capital process. (a) Post-closing statement: checklist says Buyer delivers within 90 days (August 13, 2025). APA Section 2.6(b) says 60 days, which is July 14, 2025. If Buyer follows the checklist, it misses its APA deadline by 30 days. (b) De Minimis Collar: the checklist omits the $150,000 collar. No adjustment is made if the variance is $150,000 or less. If the variance is greater, the full amount is adjusted, not just the excess (Section 2.6(d)). The checklist's "dollar-for-dollar for any deviation" is wrong. (c) Estimated adjustment: Section 2.6(a) adjusts the Closing Cash Payment at closing for the estimated NWC variance above the collar. The checklist treats the estimate as informational only (P-4) and fixes the closing wire at a flat amount (B-1). The Estimated Closing Statement is due 3 Business Days before closing. (d) Dispute mechanics: the checklist omits the 15-day Resolution Period and the independent Accounting Firm (30 days; costs split equally) in Section 2.6(c). It also cites "Section 2.6(d)" for the payment mechanics, but Section 2.6(e) governs. Action: rewrite PC-1 and PC-2.
D-7 HIGH. Holdback release timing. Checklist: within 90 days after final determination, citing Section 2.6(d). APA Section 2.5(b)(iii) says 90 days, but Section 2.6(e) says 5 Business Days. This conflict is an APA defect (Section 6). Action: docket the conservative 5-Business-Day date and obtain a clarifying amendment.
D-8 MEDIUM. Payoff funding. Checklist P-5 lists a Summit Ridge payoff wire (about $14.3 million) in the funds flow, but the B-1 total of $84,000,000 excludes it. APA Section 8.1(i) and Section 2.4(a) make the debt a Seller liability, with the payoff letter as a Seller deliverable. Neither document says whether the payoff is netted from Seller's proceeds. Action: confirm in the funds flow.
D-9 LOW. The checklist omits the Section 1060 allocation (Buyer delivers within 90 days after final NWC determination; Section 6.7(b)).

3. DATES, TERMS AND ANCILLARY AGREEMENT DEVIATIONS
D-10 CRITICAL. Outside Date. Checklist: July 14, 2025, cited to Section 9.1(b). APA: August 14, 2025, in Section 10.1(b). Termination is Article X, not Section 9.1. The checklist shortens the closing window by a month and invites a wrongful termination or tolling error.
D-11 HIGH. Reverse Break-Up Fee. The amount ($2,625,000; 3%) matches. The trigger does not. The checklist says it is payable on Seller's termination "pursuant to Section 9.1(d)". In the APA, Section 9.1(d) is the Fraud survival clause. The fee is payable only on Seller's termination under Section 10.1(e), for Buyer's failure to close when all conditions are satisfied or waived (Section 10.3).
D-12 HIGH. Transition Services Agreement. Checklist: $50,000 per month, $300,000 total. APA: $45,000 per month, $270,000 total (Section 8.1(d); Exhibit D). The term (6 months, ending November 15, 2025) matches. The services also differ. The checklist lists IT migration, customer relationship management and administration. Exhibit D lists IT support, financial reporting and accounting, HR and payroll transition, vendor relationship management and administration. The checklist overpays by $30,000 and omits the HR/payroll services.
D-13 HIGH. Non-Competition Agreement. Checklist: 3 years, expiring May 15, 2028. APA: 4 years, so expiring May 15, 2029 (Section 8.1(e); Exhibit E). Geography (United States and Canada) matches. The checklist adds customer/employee non-solicits not in the Exhibit E summary and omits its 2% passive-ownership carve-out. A 3-year form would breach Section 8.1(e).
D-14 MEDIUM. Employee matters. (a) The checklist cites Section 6.1 for employee offers. The correct cite is Section 6.8 (Section 6.1 is conduct of business). (b) Timing: APA Section 6.8(a) requires offers no later than 15 days before the Closing Date, which is April 30, 2025. The checklist says 10 business days before (about May 1). That is one day late, and the checklist is dated April 28, so the real deadline is two days away. (c) WARN: Section 6.8(c) splits responsibility. Seller is responsible for its pre-closing actions and Buyer for its post-closing actions. The checklist (PC-5) places WARN on Seller alone.
D-15 MEDIUM. PTO. The checklist cites Section 2.3(c) for the accrued PTO assumption. The correct cite is Section 2.3(d); Section 2.3(c) covers warranty obligations.
4. MISSING OR MISDESCRIBED CLOSING CONDITIONS AND DELIVERABLES
D-17 CRITICAL. Northwind consent omitted. APA Section 7.1(d)(iii) and Schedule 7.1(d), item 3 (anti-assignment clause, Section 12.3 of the Supply Agreement dated April 12, 2021) make Northwind Aerospace's consent a closing condition and a Seller deliverable. Checklist P-2 and S-9 list only Summit Ridge, Crestline and Burnham Street, plus HSR. Action: add Northwind as P-2(v) and track it. If it is not obtained, Buyer's condition fails unless waived. Section 6.4 requires the parties to agree an alternative arrangement giving Buyer the economics of the contract.
D-18 CRITICAL. FIRPTA Certificate omitted. APA Section 8.1(f) requires a certificate in the form prescribed by Treasury Regulations Section 1.1445-2(b)(2). It is also a separate closing condition under Section 7.1(h). It is not in the checklist. Add it to Part IV.
D-19 CRITICAL. Landlord estoppel certificates omitted. APA Section 7.1(f) and Section 8.1(k) require estoppels from all landlords under the Assigned Real Property Leases (at least Burnham Street). Add to Parts III and IV.
D-20 HIGH. Title insurance commitments. APA Section 8.1(l) requires Seller to deliver title commitments from Cascadia Title for the Hillsboro owned property. The checklist treats title only as a Buyer's counsel pre-closing task (P-6) awaiting a preliminary report. It is not a Seller deliverable on the checklist. Move it to Part IV and align the form with the Permitted Encumbrances standard.
D-21 HIGH. Washington good standing. Section 8.1(h) requires certificates from Oregon and Washington, each dated within 10 Business Days of closing. The checklist (S-7) lists Oregon only. Add Washington. (The checklist's "no earlier than ten (10) business days prior" is consistent with the APA.)
D-22 MEDIUM. Closing certificates overstated. Section 8.1(m) requires Seller's certificate to cover only Sections 7.1(a), (b) and (c). The checklist (S-10) says it covers all of Section 7.1, which would include the consents. Section 8.2(h) requires Buyer's certificate to cover only Sections 7.2(a) and (b). The checklist (B-7) says all of Section 7.2.
D-23 MEDIUM. Bill of Sale and real property. Section 8.1(a) and Exhibit A limit the Bill of Sale to tangible personal property. The checklist (S-1) says it conveys all of the "Acquired Assets" (the APA term is "Purchased Assets"). Neither document includes a deed or conveyance of the Hillsboro real property or an assignment of the Portland lease beyond the Assignment and Assumption Agreement. See Section 6.
D-26 MEDIUM. Secretary's Certificate (S-6). Section 8.1(g) requires certification of the Crestline consent among the resolutions, and a certificate dated as of the Closing Date. The checklist omits both. The APA names the "Second Amended and Restated" LLC Agreement.
D-27 MEDIUM. Litigation condition. The checklist (P-8) ties Aeromet to Section 7.1(g). That section concerns Governmental Authority orders or actions to enjoin the Closing, not private litigation. Aeromet is an Excluded Liability under Section 2.4(d) (correct), but a private claim does not by itself engage Section 7.1(g). Reframe as a Section 2.4(d)/9.2(c) indemnity item.
D-28 MEDIUM. Portland Lease description. The checklist calls it a "Commercial Lease Agreement dated September 1, 2019". Schedule 7.1(d) says "Lease Agreement dated February 14, 2018", with the consent right in Section 17.2 (not to be unreasonably withheld). Verify against the lease, since a wrong description in a consent request could defeat the consent.
D-29 LOW. Crestline consent. The checklist cites the "Amended and Restated" LLC Agreement. The APA says "Second Amended and Restated". Schedule 7.1(d) notes a 75% member approval threshold. Novak holds only 72%, so Crestline's consent is required (the checklist correctly includes it).

5. PARTY AND TERMINOLOGY DEVIATIONS
D-30 LOW. Seller officer title. The checklist uses "Founder and Managing Member". The APA uses "Manager" (Knowledge definition, Section 11.1, signature block). Certificates should use the APA title.
Matching items (verified): Purchase Price, Target NWC, Basket, Mini-Basket, Fundamental Cap, survival periods, Reverse Break-Up Fee amount, 108-of-127 offers, HSR dates, Escrow Agent, Aeromet exclusion.

6. APA DEFECTS REQUIRING AMENDMENT (not checklist errors)
(a) Buyer's name. The cover page and signature block say "Vanguard Industrial Holdings, Inc." The preamble, notice block and Exhibits say Saxonbrook Industrial Holdings, Inc. The Buyer's notice email domain is vanguardindustrial.com. This is a CRITICAL execution defect. Confirm the correct legal entity and, if necessary, correct by written amendment under Section 11.5 so that the signatory and the closing certificates match.
(b) Holdback release (5 Business Days in Section 2.6(e) versus 90 days in Section 2.5(b)(iii)).
(c) No deed. Section 8.1 does not require a deed for the Hillsboro owned property. Consider adding a statutory warranty deed and a recording plan. Nor is there a closing condition for the Aeromet litigation, which is a risk-allocation point.

7. RECOMMENDED PRIORITY ACTIONS
1. Confirm and correct the Buyer entity name. 2. Rebuild the funds flow: $78,750,000 / $5,250,000 / $3,500,000 holdback, with the estimated NWC adjustment and the payoff netting confirmed. 3. Add Northwind consent, FIRPTA, estoppels, title commitments and the Washington good standing. 4. Re-docket: Outside Date August 14, 2025; Proposed Final Closing Statement July 14, 2025; escrow expiry November 15, 2026; non-compete May 15, 2029; offer letters April 30, 2025. 5. Conform the TSA ($45,000 / $270,000) and the Non-Compete (4 years) to Exhibits D and E. 6. Correct all article and section cross-references (Article IX for indemnity; Article X for termination; Section 2.3(d); Section 6.8).
